title: Descent of morphisms between perfect complexes
statement: Let (R_i)_{i\in I} be a filtered system of rings with colimit R, fix i\in I, and let X_i be a finitely presented R_i-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Put X_j=X_i \times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)} \operatorname{Spec}(R_j) for j\ge i and X=X_i \times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)} \operatorname{Spec}(R). Let P_i and Q_i be perfect objects of D(O_{X_i}) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex], and write P_j,Q_j and P,Q for their derived pullbacks to X_j and X, respectively. Every morphism f:P\to Q in D(O_X) is, after replacing i by a later index j, the pullback of a morphism f_j:P_j\to Q_j; moreover, if f is an isomorphism then j may be chosen so that f_j is an isomorphism, and finitely many prescribed equalities between such morphisms hold at the same later index.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, label lemma-descend-homomorphisms (full faithfulness), used in Lemma 36.29.3, Tag 09RF

proof.text: The assertion is local on the finitely presented scheme X_i. For a quasi-compact open U_i of X_i with preimages U_j in X_j and U in X, let \mathcal P(U_i) be the condition that for every integer n the canonical map \operatorname{colim}_{j\ge i}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(O_{U_j})}(P_j|_{U_j},Q_j|_{U_j}[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(O_U)}(P|_U,Q|_U[n]) is bijective. Since X_i is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, it suffices by the induction principle for quasi-compact opens [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] to prove \mathcal P for affine opens (Step 2) and the gluing step. For the gluing step let W=U\cup V with U quasi-compact, V affine, and \mathcal P holding for U, V, U\cap V. A perfect object lies in D_{QCoh} (it is locally strictly perfect with quasi-coherent terms [def-pc-perfect-complex]; Stacks Tag 08DB), so the derived Mayer–Vietoris triangle [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle] applies to Q_j|_{W_j} on each W_j and to Q|_W on the preimage of W. Applying \operatorname{Hom}(P_j|_{W_j},-[n]) and identifying \operatorname{Hom}(P_j|_{W_j},R(j_U)_*Q_j|_{U_j}[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(P_j|_{U_j},Q_j|_{U_j}[n]) by the adjunction L j_U^*\dashv R(j_U)_* for the open immersion (where L j_U^* is restriction) [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint], and likewise for V and U\cap V, gives the long exact Mayer–Vietoris Hom sequence at each stage j and on the preimage of W; these sequences are compatible with derived pullback because pullback commutes with restriction to opens. Filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact, so the colimit of the stage sequences is exact, and the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma], applied around the term for W in degree n (whose four neighbours are terms for U, V, U\cap V in degrees n-1 and n, bijective by hypothesis), shows \mathcal P(W). The case W=X_i is the required bijection.

source.place: Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, proof: induction principle on quasi-compact opens and Mayer–Vietoris for Hom

proof.text: Affine case. Let U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i) be affine, U_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A_j) and U=\operatorname{Spec}(A) its preimages, A=\operatorname{colim}_jA_j (affine transition morphisms). P_i|_{U_i} and Q_i|_{U_i}[n] are perfect, hence in D_{QCoh} (Tag 08DB, as in Step 1), so by [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] they are isomorphic to \widetilde{E_0} and \widetilde{K_0} for bounded complexes E_0, K_0 of finite projective A_i-modules; K_0, a bounded complex of flat modules, is K-flat (Stacks Tag 0649). Since the terms are flat, the derived pullbacks to U_j and U are \widetilde{E_0\otimes_{A_i}A_j}, \widetilde{K_0\otimes_{A_i}A_j} and \widetilde{E_0\otimes_{A_i}A}, \widetilde{K_0\otimes_{A_i}A}. The equivalence D(A)\simeq D_{QCoh}(O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}) [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] (D_{QCoh} being a full subcategory) identifies the Hom sets in D(O_{U_j}) and D(O_U) with those in D(A_j) and D(A), compatibly with the transition maps, and the affine calculation [lem-pc-affine-perfect-hom-colimit] then gives the bijection \mathcal P(U_i).

source.place: Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, affine case in the proof

proof.text: By Step 1 with n=0 the map \operatorname{colim}_j\operatorname{Hom}(P_j,Q_j)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q) is bijective: surjectivity gives the factorization f=Lf^*f_j, and injectivity gives that two morphisms at stage j with equal pullbacks become equal at a later stage; by filteredness finitely many prescribed equalities hold at one common later stage. If f is an isomorphism, apply the same to Q,P (also perfect) to choose g:Q_j\to P_j representing f^{-1} at a common stage. The composites g\circ f_j and f_j\circ g pull back to identities, so after one further increase of j both are identities; hence f_j is an isomorphism.
